blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Profit and cash look similar, but they are very different. Profit is what you earned on paper. Cash is the money you actually have in the bank. A company can be profitable and still run out of cash. This happens when customers pay late, or when big costs come before the money arrives.

At Czarnikow, this matters every day. The trading desk can close a good sugar deal today. However, the cash from that deal might not arrive for 60 or 90 days. Meanwhile, the company still needs to pay suppliers, freight and salaries.

Understanding the gap between profit and cash is very important. Many companies do not fail because they are unprofitable. They fail because they run out of cash at the wrong moment.

items.q: What is cash, according to the text?
options: The money you actually have in the bank
The money you earned on paper
The number of clients you have
items.why: "Cash is the money you actually have in the bank."

items.q: Why can a profitable company still run out of cash?
options: Because customers pay late or big costs come first
Because it never earns any profit
Because it closes too many deals
items.why: "This happens when customers pay late, or when big costs come before the money arrives."

items.q: At Czarnikow, when might the cash from a good deal arrive?
items.why: "the cash from that deal might not arrive for 60 or 90 days."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Profit and cash are different things
A profitable company is always safe
Cash is needed to pay salaries
Late payments can create a cash gap
items.why: Inferência: o texto mostra que uma empresa lucrativa pode falir por falta de caixa, então "sempre segura" está errado.

items.q: The last paragraph suggests that…
options: profit is the only thing that matters
cash problems can be more dangerous than low profit
items.why: Inferência: muitas empresas falem por falta de caixa, não por falta de lucro — o caixa é o risco imediato.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver falando com um novo colega de vendas. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Let me explain one thing early, because it is easy to get wrong.

You just closed a big deal. Well done. On paper, it looks great, and yes, it is profitable. But the client pays in 90 days. So the profit is real, but the cash is not here yet. That is a big difference.

This month, we still have to pay our suppliers. We have to pay freight for the sugar. We have to pay salaries, including yours. All of that needs cash, not profit. Profit does not pay the bills. Cash pays the bills.

So when you look at a deal, do not only ask, "Is it profitable?" Also ask, "When does the money arrive?" A deal with fast payment can help us more this month than a bigger deal with 90-day terms.

I am not saying long-term deals are bad. They are fine. However, we must always watch the cash. Many good companies fail, not because they lose money, but because one day there is no cash in the bank. Keep that in your head, and you will do very well here.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Oliver say the new deal's cash is "not here yet"?
options: Because the deal is not profitable
Because the client pays in 90 days
Because the client cancelled the deal
Because there is no sugar to sell
items.why: "the client pays in 90 days. So the profit is real, but the cash is not here yet."

items.q: According to Oliver, what pays the bills this month?
items.why: "Profit does not pay the bills. Cash pays the bills."

items.q: What second question does Oliver want you to ask about a deal?
items.why: "Also ask, 'When does the money arrive?'"

items.q: What can we infer about Oliver's view of long-term deals?
options: He thinks they are always bad
He accepts them, but wants people to watch the cash
He wants to stop all sugar deals
He only likes deals over 90 days
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que os contratos longos são "fine", mas insiste em vigiar o caixa.

items.q: Why does Oliver say many good companies fail?
options: Because they lose money every month
Because one day there is no cash in the bank
items.why: Inferência: "not because they lose money, but because one day there is no cash in the bank."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The deal looks good on paper, but the money is not here yet." On paper means…
options: in theory, or in the numbers
items.why: On paper = no papel, na teoria/nos números — pode ser diferente da realidade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We have the profit, but we must ___ 90 days for the cash."
items.why: To wait = esperar. Precisamos esperar 90 dias pelo dinheiro.

items.q: A customer is…
options: a person or company that buys from you
a person who works in your team
items.why: Customer = cliente, quem compra de você.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If a company runs out of cash, it can ___."
items.why: To fail = falir; ficar sem caixa pode levar a empresa à falência.

items.q: "Profit is an opinion, but cash is a fact." A fact is…
items.why: Fact = fato, algo real; o caixa no banco é um número concreto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões de negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The client did not pay, so the money is late. We are still waiting on them." To wait on someone means to…
options: wait for them to do something
items.why: Wait on = esperar que alguém faça algo (aqui, pagar).

items.q: "The company almost ran out of cash last month." To run out of something means to…
items.why: Run out of = acabar, ficar sem. Quase ficaram sem caixa.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the new deal." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We must keep an eye on the cash every week." To keep an eye on means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, vigiar de perto.

items.q: "Cash problems can add up and become very serious." To add up means to…
items.why: Add up = ir somando, acumular até virar um problema grande.
